name: Juquila Mixe
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Wichmann, Soren. 1995. The Relationship Among the Mixe-Zoquean Languages of Mexico (comparative phonological data on Mixe varieties incl. Juquila; not readable online)

new_statements.quote: ACENTO. El acento tónico carga generalmente en la sílaba radical de la palabra; si esta es compuesta conserva el acento en la palabra principal del compuesto, como: uóp, azotar; pauóp, arrear; tukpauóp, hacer arrear; en las cuales el acento tónico está en la palabra uóp.
new_statements.translation: ACCENT. Tonic stress generally falls on the root syllable of the word; if the word is a compound, it keeps the stress on the principal word of the compound, e.g. uóp 'to whip'; pauóp 'to drive (animals)'; tukpauóp 'to make (someone) drive'; in all of which the tonic stress is on the word uóp.
new_statements.citation: Belmar, Francisco. 1902. Lenguas indígenas del Estado de Oaxaca: Estudio del idioma ayook. Oaxaca: Imprenta del Comercio.
new_statements.locator: Estudio (grammar part), section 'ACENTO.', p. 7 (archive.org scan estudiodelidioma01belm, PDF p. 49; verified on the rendered page image Belmar1902_pages/)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the root syllable (Mixe roots are mostly monosyllabic; affixes such as pa-, tuk- are unstressed); in compounds and derived words the stress stays on the head root, e.g. tuk-pa-uóp.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (simple and compound/derived words); no remarks on phrase stress or citation forms. Belmar's data mix Quintana's colonial Juquila ('mohtuau') Mixe with Villa Alta (Totontepec-area) material, so the statement is a 1902 pan-'ayook' generalisation rather than a modern description of Juquila proper.
new_statements.identity_note: Belmar 1902 is filed by Glottolog under juqu1238 ('Midland Mixe in Juquila'), but Belmar explicitly draws on Quintana's colonial Juquila Mixe ('dialecto mohtuau... de Juquila') and on the Villa Alta (Totontepec-area, toto1263) variety, so his accent rule is a pan-'ayook' statement. Glottolog 5 places Chuxnabán Mixe (chux1234; Jany's and Dagostino's 'Chuxnabán Mixe', ISO pxm, mun. Quetzaltepec) as a dialect of juqu1238, so Jany 2011 (held under../quet1239/) and Dagostino 2025 are first-hand for this languoid but give no placement rule. The SIL mxq-tagged Miller 1947 manuscripts are based on San Lucas Camotlán data. Santos Martínez 2013 ('mixe de Metepec') describes an agencia of Totontepec (toto1263), not this language.

sources.citation: Santos Martínez, María del Rosario. 2013. El sistema fonológico del mixe de Metepec: aspectos segmentales y prosódicos. Tesis de maestría en Lingüística Indoamericana, CIESAS, México.
sources.note: NOT this language: San Miguel Metepec is an agencia of Totontepec Villa de Morelos, 'Mixe alto del norte' (pp. 6-9) = Totontepec Mixe (toto1263). Its rule (sec. 4.4, p. 233): stress on the final syllable when it has a long, long-glottalised or rearticulated vowel, otherwise on the penult (moraic trochee built from the right edge).
